atoms.text: A trial by ordeal was overseen by a priest or holy man. The idea of the trial was to have God indicate if the accused was guilty or not.
One example was trial by water, where a man was tied up and thrown into a lake or river. If he floated, he was guilty; if he sank, he was innocent.

atoms.a: Why do you think a trial by water might not be fair?
b: ++The person could easily drown even if they were found innocent.
The person had too many lawyers.
The person was not allowed to swim butterfly.

feedback.end: Trials by ordeal are not very fair by modern standards. Many of the ordeals could result in very serious injury, even if the person was found to be innocent!
